title: State file persisted via temp file, fsync and atomic rename
source: Authored for the CodeReview benchmark corpus (expanded clean stratum), 2026-11-05
false_flag_note: A reviewer may flag the temp file or the os.replace as over-engineering, or the directory fsync as a bug. The pattern is the correct one: the temp file lives in the same directory (same filesystem, so the rename is atomic), the file is flushed and fsynced before the rename, a failed write unlinks the temp file and re-raises, and fsyncing the directory afterwards is what makes the rename itself durable across a crash.
